name: Double shear layer
blurb: Two thin shear layers in a doubly periodic box of liquid at Mach 0.1, kicked sideways: each rolls up into a vortex. Too coarse a grid grows spurious vortices along the braids between them (Bell, Colella & Glaz 1989), so it shows how a scheme behaves when under-resolved.

featured.label: Sound speed
featured.tip: The liquid's sound speed. The flow's speed is 1, so the Mach number is 1 over this: at 10 the density stays within 1% of its reference and the flow is incompressible to that accuracy. The step shrinks in proportion as it grows

featured.label: Layer sharpness
featured.tip: The layers' inverse thickness, in box sides: 30 is the thick layer of the original test, 80 to 100 the thin one

featured.label: Viscosity
featured.tip: Kinematic viscosity (the original thin-layer test used 0.0002 to 0.00005)
